one_line: A 7-second single-shot clip of a glaring, doll-like toddler girl with red lipstick and a gold watch, holding an old mobile phone to her ear like an angry adult, who breaks into a big grin at the end.

hook.visual: Static front-on shot of a chubby toddler in pigtails and a floral dress, scowling sideways with an old candy-bar phone at her ear, one hand on her hip, a gold wristwatch on her wrist.
hook.why_it_stops_the_scroll: The first frame already contains the whole gag: a toddler styled and posed like an irritated adult on a phone call (lipstick, watch, hand on hip), readable with the sound off.

beats.observed: Toddler glares to the side, phone at ear, lips closed, red lipstick.
Brow furrowed, mouth open as if shouting into the phone.
Looks straight at camera, pouting mouth in an 'o' shape, still frowning.
Stern stare with pursed lips, body unchanged from earlier frames.
beats.spoken: Papagai Penie! (unreliable, may be babble or a Whisper error)

beats.observed: Face switches to a wide open-mouth grin with squinted happy eyes while holding the same pose.

payoff: The scowl turns into a big grin at about 6.0s, one second before the clip ends.
share_or_comment_trigger: Parents and grandparents sending it to the person who 'sounds like this on the phone'; the tiny runtime also invites replays. Comment count is not in meta.json.
why_it_worked: Outlier_x 4,039.8: 29,490,888 views against a channel median of 7,300, so the clip was pushed far beyond the channel's usual audience, likely by the Shorts feed (inferred).
7 seconds and one shot make it very easy to finish and replay; the grin at 6.0s gives a clear mini-payoff (inferred; no retention data).
180,653 likes is 0.61% of views, a modest rate that fits a feed-pushed passive audience more than a loyal one (inference).
paid_signal: unclear: like_rate 0.61% is above the 0.3% paid-looking threshold, so no strong sign; the huge outlier on a small channel could be feed distribution or promotion and I cannot tell.

solo_route.how: 1) Take a still of a LumeBook illustrated child hero (fictional) or generate a toddler character in the same style. 2) Use image-to-video to make a 6 to 7 second single shot: the child holds a toy phone to the ear, scowls, then grins at the last second; ask for a locked camera. 3) Add either an AI child-like voice or your own babble over it, and no on-screen text or a 3-word Hebrew line. 4) End on a 1 second LumeBook end card. Total about 7 seconds, 3 to 6 generations to get a clean one.
solo_route.needs: Nothing, if you use LumeBook's own illustrated hero. Avoid the lipstick and adult styling on a toddler, and avoid a real child's photo as the source.
